blocks.title: set
bullets: In math, a set is a collection of values without any duplicates.

blocks.title: set Example
blocks.code:
students = [
    {"name": "Hermione", "house": "Gryffindor"},
    {"name": "Harry", "house": "Gryffindor"},
    {"name": "Ron", "house": "Gryffindor"},
    {"name": "Draco", "house": "Slytherin"},
    {"name": "Padma", "house": "Ravenclaw"},
]

houses = set()
for student in students:
    houses.add(student["house"])

for house in sorted(houses):
    print(house)
blocks.expectedOutput: Run this code to see the result.

blocks.title: set
blocks.body: The `set` object takes care of eliminating duplicates for us automatically.
bullets: You can learn more in Python's documentation of [`set`](https://docs.python.org/3/library/stdtypes.html#set).

blocks.title: Global Variables
bullets: We can leverage global variables within Python. To interact with a global variable inside a function, use the `global` keyword:

blocks.title: Global Variables Example
blocks.code:
balance = 0


def main():
    print("Balance:", balance)
    deposit(100)
    withdraw(50)
    print("Balance:", balance)


def deposit(n):
    global balance
    balance += n


def withdraw(n):
    global balance
    balance -= n


if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
blocks.expectedOutput: Run this code to see the result.

blocks.title: Docstrings
bullets: A standard way of commenting your function's purpose is to use a docstring:

blocks.title: Docstrings Example
blocks.code:
def meow(n):
    """
    Meow n times.

    :param n: Number of times to meow
    :type n: int
    :raise TypeError: If n is not an int
    :return: A string of n meows, one per line
    :rtype: str
    """
    return "meow\n" * n


number = int(input("Number: "))
meows = meow(number)
print(meows, end="")
blocks.expectedOutput: Run this code to see the result.

blocks.title: argparse
bullets: `argparse` is a library that handles all the parsing of complicated command-line arguments:

blocks.title: argparse Example
blocks.code:
import argparse

parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Meow like a cat")
parser.add_argument("-n", default=1, help="number of times to meow", type=int)
args = parser.parse_args()

for _ in range(args.n):
    print("meow")
blocks.expectedOutput: Run this code to see the result.

blocks.title: args and kwargs
bullets: We can tell a function to expect an unknown number of positional arguments (`*args`) and keyword arguments (`**kwargs`):

blocks.title: args and kwargs Example
blocks.code:
def f(*args, **kwargs):
    print("Positional:", args)
    print("Named:", kwargs)


f(100, 50, 25)
f(galleons=100, sickles=50, knuts=25)

blocks.title: args and kwargs
blocks.body: `args` are positional arguments; `kwargs` are named ("keyword") arguments.

blocks.title: List Comprehensions
bullets: List comprehensions allow you to create a list on the fly in one elegant one-liner:

blocks.title: List Comprehensions Example
blocks.code:
students = [
    {"name": "Hermione", "house": "Gryffindor"},
    {"name": "Harry", "house": "Gryffindor"},
    {"name": "Ron", "house": "Gryffindor"},
    {"name": "Draco", "house": "Slytherin"},
]

gryffindors = [
    student["name"] for student in students if student["house"] == "Gryffindor"
]

for gryffindor in sorted(gryffindors):
    print(gryffindor)
blocks.expectedOutput: Run this code to see the result.

blocks.title: filter
bullets: `filter` returns a subset of a sequence for which a certain condition is true:

blocks.title: filter Example
blocks.code:
students = [
    {"name": "Hermione", "house": "Gryffindor"},
    {"name": "Harry", "house": "Gryffindor"},
    {"name": "Ron", "house": "Gryffindor"},
    {"name": "Draco", "house": "Slytherin"},
]

gryffindors = filter(lambda s: s["house"] == "Gryffindor", students)

for gryffindor in sorted(gryffindors, key=lambda s: s["name"]):
    print(gryffindor["name"])
blocks.expectedOutput: Run this code to see the result.

Your `main` function and your custom functions must be in a file called `project.py` in the root of your project; your tests must be in `test_project.py`.
